_note: Written pages: the writing need (data/world/needs.json) is met by a scribe writing on a surface with ink, so scribes get demand from literate people's use of writing. One recipe for each surface; the household mix chooses among them.

written_page_papyrus.basis: per written page of a letter, account or copied text on papyrus
written_page_papyrus.yield_basis: A page takes one sheet of the writing surface and about a tenth of a gram of ink (see the ink figure below). A scribe in a book hand wrote a few pages a day: Lithub, 'Writing as spiritual practice: inside the world of medieval scribes' (https://lithub.com/writing-as-spiritual-practice-inside-the-world-of-medieval-scribes/, opened): 'A professional scribe could complete about three to four pages per day', which in an eight-hour day is two to 2.7 hours a page; taken here as three hours (a little slow, allowing for ruling and quill cutting); document hands were quicker. Services that turn materials into what households use are recipes on the trades that do the work, as the laid walls are. Pass 11 ink: onepenshow.com, ink economy (https://hn.jakechampion.name/reader/https://onepenshow.com/ink/economy, opened) measured fountain pens at 0.016 ml a page (fine nib), 0.04 (medium) and 0.05 (broad), from one test of three pens, so about 0.05 g a page at 1 g/ml; a folio in a dense book hand carries about twice a notebook page's writing (our assumption), so 0.1 g, taken as 0.0001 kg (was 0.0015 kg, fifteen times the sourced figure, so changed; a fountain pen is the modern analogue of a quill, and a quill's dip loss is not counted). Round 2 quill check: artcalcs.uk, Calligraphy ink volume calculator (https://artcalcs.uk/calligraphy/ink-volume-calculator/, opened) models a typical A4 page with a 2 mm broad-edge nib at 'roughly 0.2-0.4 ml including waste' (3.5 strokes a character, ink film 0.008 to 0.015 mm, 40 percent waste for loading and drips; it calls its figures rules of thumb, not measurements, and says broad-edge writing uses 'several times more ink per character' than the 0.016 to 0.05 ml fountain-pen figures). At 1 g/ml that is 0.2 to 0.4 g a page, 2 to 4 times the 0.1 g here; the middle, 0.3 g, is 3 times. The waste part is dip residue largely returned to the pot, so the net is nearer 0.12 to 0.24 g, within 3x of 0.1 g, so the value is kept (a modelled figure; no measured quill figure was found: the Straight Dope thread, boards.straightdope.com/t/how-much-can-you-write-with-a-quill-pen-on-a-single-ink-dip/749494, opened, only says about one line of textura or three to six words a dip, with no ink volume). Every figure in this row now has an opened source or one stated arithmetic step, confidence C.

Paper sheet mass: papersizes.org, Weight of sheets (https://www.papersizes.org/weight-of-sheets.htm, opened) gives an A4 sheet at 80 gsm as 5 g, which is where the 0.005 kg comes from (modern machine paper as the analogue for a hand-made sheet). The desk and tools (timber, iron, carpenter hours, life) have no source found, so the row stays D. Round 2 (Pass 12): Humphrey, Regional Furniture Society Journal xxxv, 2021 (https://regionalfurnituresociety.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/02-rfsj-2021-humphrey.pdf, opened): an English oak desk cupboard of 1430 to 1450, 98 cm high, 86.8 cm wide, 56 cm deep, boards with 25 mm grooves and uprights close to 3 inches square. With 25 mm boards (our reading of the 25 mm groove height) the box's 3.8 square metres of faces give 0.094 cubic metres plus 0.025 for the four uprights, about 0.12 cubic metres, against 0.3 here (2.5 times, within 3x, kept). Carpenter hours, iron and life remain unsourced. Round 3 (Pass 13): Follansbee, 'thoughts on hand tools and green wood' (https://pfollansbee.wordpress.com/2012/09/13/thoughts-on-hand-tools-and-green-wood/, opened): an experienced joiner makes an oak joined chest by hand in 'about 60-75 hours' (a first chest took 'a couple hundred hours'). A desk cupboard of about the same board volume (0.12 cubic metres here, a chest being a comparable box; our comparison, a modern analogue) at 40 carpenter hours is within 3x of that, kept. Iron (2 kg) and the 20-year life have no source; the surviving 1430 to 1450 desk cupboard only shows a life of centuries, a floor that does not fix the figure. Stays D.

capital.good: scribe's desk, ruling tools and ink-horn
capital.capital_basis: A scribe copies a page in the three hours the entry states, so one desk turns out about seven hundred pages in a working year; the desk and tools are a plank table, a stool and a few knives, and the item states them so the writing office is not treated as plant-free.
